body: I'm not sure it's a good idea to have windows specific code in these files, should probably be handled differently

True, I removed OS specific implementation and turned the Caption buttons into generic buttons what would serve later for a linux implementation too, by passing the commands up the chain.

Also extracted the Captions Buttons to their own class, so it doesn't pollute editor_title_bar, and it becomes simpler to style just the buttons later if necessary to keep the editor style consistent.

Commit 4cd0da9511571a2035dce93e368da60e662d93ac

There is only a single #ifdef WINDOWS_ENABLED, just to ensure we only add the buttons to the titlebar if we are on Windows, as Linux isn't implemented yet, and MacOS doesn't require custom Caption Buttons.
consider dynamically loading function `GetSystemMetricsForDpi` here to support DPI scaling.
I think that this label should be visible in expand-to-title mode (this label was added exclusively for this mode).

Seems like a good idea, but the problem is where to put it. The Titlebar is already too crowded.
One option is to put it on the start of the titlebar, collapse the menu, and only show the menu when you hover the project name.
Other option is to add it on the left side of the engine version, on the status bar.

Added in c08dfd2b101c0146a0222e8e16ddaf27babddd7a
I tested in both the old version with GetSystemMetrics and the new one with GetSystemMetricsForDpi with multiple DPIs and couldn't notice a difference, but lets keep it for correctness sake.
Thank you!

It seems on MacOS, which already had expand to title, it doesn't add the title anywhere on the window. It is probably only used on the MacOS integrated titlebar. Image from the 4.6 release announcement page:
Yeah, it is strange, I was sure it is shown on MacOS...
macOS show title only when no menu is shown (which is default, normally global system menu is used): No menu (title is visible): Full menu: Collapsed menu:

Thank you!
Considering on Windows the menu is either Full (default) or collapsed (through the setting: interface/editor/appearance/collapse_main_menu) I don't think there is a situation where the menu would be hidden on Windows, since it doesn't have a unified system bar, like MacOS and sometimes Linux window managers do.
